# A struct that folds through the optimizer's value model comes back as the
# checker built it: the declaration it names, the fields in the order they were
# written, and the defaults the checker filled in after them.
#
# It used to come back as a bare map, so the literal was rebuilt with its keys
# in alphabetical order and with the entry the interpreter tagged the value's
# type in — `__type: "Point"`, a field the struct does not have and Go will not
# compile.
#
# The struct is returned by a function so the fold has to go through a value:
# a literal written in place is not re-derived from one. It is read into a
# component var so it survives as an initializer rather than being measured and
# discarded.

sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --out=out app.sngl
grep 'Point\{Y: 1, X: 7, Tag: "none"\}' out/model.go
! grep '__type' out/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"

struct Point {
    x int
    y int
    tag string = "none"
}

func origin() => Point{y = 1, x = 7}

component main {
    var here = origin()

    text(value="{string(here.x)}")
}
